notes:
Summary: Large fintech platform evaluating dedicated GPU pool for customer-facing assistants and real-time personalization. Primary focus is hard SLOs for 99.95% uptime, 95th percentile p95 < 120ms gen-latency for short prompts, predictable reserved GPU capacity for peak hours (US Eastern), and an SLA credit schedule they can accept for regulatory reporting.

Key quotes: "We cannot take more than 1 outage hour per quarter — auditors will flag us." — Head of Platform.

Tone of conversations: pragmatic, cost-aware, high bar for operational guarantees. Legal is sensitive to force majeure and maintenance windows. Ops wants explicit node replacement timelines and capacity warm standby policy.

Decision drivers: latency SLO, quantized model support (INT8/4), deterministic fallbacks for capacity exhaustion, clear credit remediation, and audit-ready uptime reports.

Notes from meeting 2026-03-05: Redwood proposed 99.9% with tiered credits; customer pushing for 99.95% and faster RTOs. SE asked for production trace logs for 2-week baseline. POC target: 4-week dedicated pilot during business hours with synthetic and replay traffic.
timeline: 2025-11-10 - Intro call (AE+SE) — initial use-case mapping, interested in dedicated pool
2025-12-02 - Security questionnaire submitted (ISO/SOC items) — awaiting appendix response
2026-01-19 - Architecture review w/ infra team — discussed VPC egress and KMS key management
2026-02-28 - Kickoff call (POC scoping) — agreed on pilot window and metrics
2026-03-05 - SLA deep dive (legal + ops + Redwood) — contested uptime and credits
2026-03-09 - Benchmarks delivered by Redwood (internal lab) — initial p95 95ms on test model, throughput numbers provided
slo_requirements: Target: 99.95% monthly uptime (aim); fallback acceptable 99.9% with enhanced credits. Latency SLO: p95 gen < 120ms for 256-token average prompts on dedicated x8 GPU pool. Throughput: sustain 250 concurrent qps during peak 09:00-17:00 ET with <5% tail amplification.
reserved_capacity_plan: Request: 8 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) reserved for core workloads, + 2 hot-standby GPUs for failover. Autoscale burst allowed up to +30% for 1 hour/day. Need predictable start-up time for burst nodes <= 90s.
maintenance_windows_preference: Prefer pre-approved monthly maintenance window: Sundays 02:00-04:00 ET. No unscheduled maintenance during business hours. Require 72-hour notice for planned maintenance that may affect latency or capacity.
sla_credit_schedule_proposal: Customer proposes: if uptime < 99.95% but >= 99.9%: 10% monthly credit; <99.9% but >=99.5%: 25% credit; <99.5%: 50% credit + executive escalation. Redwood initial offer: 99.9% with 10% credit below target. Legal to reconcile force majeure and maintenance carve-outs.
support_response_requirements: Priority 1 (system down): 15-min ack, 1-hour remediation SLA for impact reduction. Priority 2 (degraded latency/throughput): 30-min ack, 4-hour mitigation plan. 24/7 NOC required for enterprise tier. Agent: dedicated TAM preferred.
poc_scope_and_metrics: 4-week pilot in US-EAST region, traffic replay of last production day + synthetic peak. Success criteria: p95 latency <120ms, no error rate >0.5% during peak, measured throughput >=250 qps sustained for 1 hour. Deliverable: weekly runbooks + end-of-POC SLO report.
commercial_notes: Customer expects a committed monthly minimum; pricing to include reserved capacity discount and negotiated credit caps. Wants line-item for extended data retention in audit logs. Finance will run TCO model comparing 3-year reserved vs burstable pricing.
legal_notes: Open items: maintenance window definition, credit calculation method (per-month vs per-incident), SLA measurement agents (Redwood telemetry vs third-party probe), cap on credits (e.g., one month of fees), and data residency appendix.
next_meeting: 2026-03-17 - Legal + Redwood to reconcile SLA wording; ops to agree on warm-standby procedure
open_questions: Can Redwood commit to node replacement RTO <= 2 hours for HW failures?
How are credits calculated for partial-day outages (per-minute accrual)?
Can maintenance windows be limited to 1x/month and capped at 2 hours?
Is there a dedicated TAM included at enterprise tier or add-on?
